tier_reason: First-party benchmarks.md compares Model Streamer with the HF safetensors loader and Tensorizer on GP3, IO2 and S3 with versions and AWS instance stated, but no benchmark code path, CPU model or build flags; first-party with partial methodology is C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: GP3 SSD: 14.34 s at concurrency 16 vs 47.99 s for the safetensors loader (3.3x, derived from page data); concurrency 1 matches safetensors at 47.56 s. IO2 SSD: 7.53 s at concurrency 8 vs 47 s for safetensors (6.2x, derived from page data). S3: 4.88 s at concurrency 32 vs Tensorizer 37.36 s. vLLM ready time GP3 35.08 s vs 66.13 s, IO2 28.28 s vs 62.69 s.
corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark from 2024 versions (Model Streamer 0.6.0, vLLM 0.5.5, CUDA 12.4), CPU model and flags not stated, no benchmark scripts linked. The GP3 result hit the volume's 1 GiB/s cap, so it measures concurrency against a throttled disk. The InstantTensor-table figure (9.29 s vs 57.4 s) in the search record is not on this page and was dropped. The repository moved in September 2026 to dsx-ai-factory/model-streamer (the run-ai URL resolves there). The package is a Python SDK over a C++ core. Tier C.

notes: All GP3/IO2/S3/vLLM numbers verified in the Appendix tables of docs/src/benchmarks.md. Repo moved to github.com/dsx-ai-factory/model-streamer; orchestrator may want to update repo_url/id. Stars 383, Apache-2.0, last commit 2026-10-05 confirmed.

tier_reason: README Performance table (author's own run on Westmere Xeon 2.1GHz, FreeBSD/ZFS) compares LineReader with std read_until/read_line/lines; no benchmark code path, compiler version or flags stated, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: next_batch 0.27 s (38.3M lines/s) vs read_until 1.94 s (5.3M lines/s), read_line 2.54 s, lines() 3.23 s; like-for-like per-line next_line 1.51 s vs read_until 1.94 s (1.28x, derived from page data). Raw read() with no line splitting is 0.25 s.
corrections.caveats: Baseline is the Rust standard library BufRead, not POSIX read. next_batch returns a slice of all complete lines in the buffer, so its 7x over read_until is not a per-line comparison; the per-line next_line gain is about 1.28x. Lines longer than the buffer are split. No benchmark harness or flags published. Abandoned since 2019; author notes bstr 0.2.8+ for_byte_line should perform similarly.

notes: Numbers match README. Claim corrected to flag the batch-vs-line apples-to-oranges comparison. MIT, 26 stars, last commit 2019-09-13 confirmed.
